name: Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons (Siegfried Engelmann) — Parts 1 & 2

principles: Scripted lessons — parent reads the script exactly as written
Modified orthography (special letter markings) in early lessons
Mastery-based progression — don't advance until skill is solid
Blending from the first lesson (no letter-name teaching first)
Based on Engelmann's Direct Instruction research

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Direct Instruction Reading (Engelmann/DISTAR)
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Scripted, systematic phonics program. 100 sequential lessons, 20 min/day. Modified orthography fades over time. Research-backed mastery approach.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons Format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Scripted parent-led reading lessons. Each lesson: sound introduction → blending → word reading → story reading. Modified letters (macrons, joined letters) gradually transition to standard print.

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: One lesson per day, 5 days/week. Each lesson follows the same script format. 20 weeks to completion.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: built into each lesson (corrections and review)

notes: 234MB total across 2 parts (122MB + 112MB). This is THE classic reading instruction book — Engelmann's 'Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons' is one of the most widely used and research-backed reading programs. Aless asking Cosmo to 'ingest' this specifically suggests she's considering it for her kids. The Direct Instruction methodology is fundamentally different from Montessori or Charlotte Mason — it's scripted, explicit, and mastery-based. CamScanner scans.
